thread.title: Parents demand answers after Johnston school bus pickup, drop-off delays - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Parents demand answers after Johnston school bus pickup, drop-off delays - NewsBreak

author: Kysha Hancock
title: Parents demand answers after Johnston school bus pickup, drop-off delays - NewsBreak
text:
By Kysha Hancock Lauren Brill ,
5 hours ago
JOHNSTON, R.I. (WPRI) — It's safe to say it's been a rocky start to the school year in Johnston.
Students at Johnston Public Schools returned to the classroom Wednesday morning, but not without headaches caused by the district's new school bus service.
Several parents told 12 News that some of the buses arrived late to pick their children up for school. For some parents, the buses didn't show up at all.
Johnston parent Ali Novak explained that she received a voice message from the district prior to the first day of school regarding the new bus routes and schedule.
In the voice message, Novak said the district explained that the new bus drivers had just finished up their final practice routes, and Zum — the new school bus service — would be providing families with their students' bussing assignments.
"We got this message after five o'clock [Tuesday] night, basically stating, 'Don't worry, the buses are going to be figured out and you might get a message after 8 p.m.,'" Novak said. "This is, again, the day before school starts. 'You might get a message.'"
Novak said she never received a bus number for her son. She initially sent him to the bus stop that her neighbor's child was given in hopes that her son would get to school on time.
Instead, she decided to drive him to school herself after waiting 45 minutes for the bus to show up.
In response to Novak's situation, Johnston Public Schools shared with 12 News a letter it sent to families about mechanical issues that delayed Bus #519, which couldn't leave the bus yard until 10 a.m.
That letter also referenced problems with Zum's app, which is supposed to allow parents and guardians to track their children's pickups and drop-offs.
"The application needs to recognize [your child's daycare] as your child's designated pickup/drop-off location rather than your home address," Johnston Superintendent Scott Sutherland explained. "Zum is prioritizing this correction, and our technology department is working directly with their team."
"Although your child's pickup was confirmed in our transportation system, that information was not properly reflected in the parent-facing application," Sutherland's letter to Bus #519 families continued. "This is part of the issue we are working with Zum to correct today. Once corrected, families should be able to use the Zum application to properly track their child's bus transportation."
Zum also sent 12 News a blog post that said in part, "Zum's operations and routing teams are working closely with JPS, monitoring routes in real time and making targeted adjustments to timing, stops and schedules. We will continue using real-world operating data to improve performance and reliability each day."
The district's busing situation escalated after the final bell rang Wednesday afternoon, when several parents told 12 News their children were stuck on school buses for hours waiting to be brought home.
Melissa Cameron said her daughter is a third grader at the new Johnston Elementary School. Her daughter, who's 8 years old and has Down syndrome, was supposed to be dropped off at a nearby daycare, but the bus was two hours late.
"She has special [requirements] in her [Individualized Education Program] — she has to be toileted every hour," Cameron explained before her daughter was dropped off.
June Santoro, whose son is in third grade at Winsor Hill Elementary School, was also extremely concerned for her child's safety.
"Is he scared? Is he crying? Is he sleeping? Is he even going to get dropped off at the right place?" Santoro questioned. "I'm frustrated. You not only have my child, but everybody's children sitting on these buses for all these hours."
Santoro said her son was eventually dropped off behind schedule at their home, even though he was also supposed to be brought to the same daycare as Cameron's daughter.
In a voicemail to families Wednesday night, Sutherland acknowledged that Zum's app was not recognizing the correct pickup and drop-off locations, as well as bus assignments.
Sutherland also explained that the district reviewed what happened and made "significant improvements" for Thursday.
"We sincerely appreciate your patience as we work through the challenges that naturally come with the first day," Sutherland said in the message.
Sutherland asked parents not to arrive more than 10 minutes before the start of school or dismissal to ensure that buses can easily drop students off and pick them up.
"Keeping the roadway clear and following the 10-minute drop-off window will make a significant difference," he added.
